chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, Abu Saeed, al-Adami, al-Razi.

He was weak in hadith, not relied upon in it. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa attested to ghuluw (exaggeration) and lying against him, and exiled him from Qum to Rayy, and he used to reside in it. He had corresponded with Abu Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon him) upon the hand of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, for the middle of Rabi' al-Akhir in the year 255.

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ الْعَسْكَرِيُّ: Abu Muhammad al-Askari (Imam Hasan al-Askari, the 10th Imam)
key_terms.الرَّيُّ: Rayy (a city near Tehran, place of exile)
key_terms.الْغُلُوُّ: ghuluw (exaggeration in the virtues of the Imams)
key_terms.رَبِيعَ الْآخِرِ: Rabi' al-Akhir (the fourth month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.قُمٌّ: Qum (a major city in Iran and center of Shia scholarship)

ai.seo_question: Who was Sahl ibn Ziyad and what was his status in hadith narration?
ai.summary: This biographical entry describes Sahl ibn Ziyad, a narrator known for being weak in hadith transmission. It notes that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa criticized him for ghuluw and lying, leading to his exile from Qum to Rayy, and records his correspondence with Imam al-Askari (AS) in 255 AH.

en.tashayyu: 63 – Sahl b. Ziyād, Abū Saʿīd al-Ādamī, al-Rāzī.

He was weak in ḥadīth, not relied upon in it.  Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā attested to ghulw and lying against him, and exiled him from Qum to Rayy, and he used to reside in it.  He had corresponded with Abū Muḥammad al-ʿAskarī upon the hand of Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-ʿAṭṭār, for the middle of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir in the year 255.
